frase_inicial: Timothy and Melanie: your spare cash, a high-rate card and thin life cover are deciding how safe your family will be.

tarjetas.frente: Big cash cushion is already working for you
tarjetas.reverso: You have a healthy bank buffer that would pay the bills if something short-term goes wrong. That same cash gives you choices about debt, protection and the kids' education without touching retirement savings.

tarjetas.frente: The high-interest card is the thing dragging your score
tarjetas.reverso: Carrying that card at a high rate costs you every month and keeps the plan capped until fixed. Using part of your cushion to cut it changes your position quickly and reduces wasted interest.

tarjetas.frente: Life insurance for both of you is the other limiter
tarjetas.reverso: Neither Timothy nor Melanie has enough life cover for two young kids to keep things running if an earner were lost. Adding cover protects Liam and Josh and lifts the plan once the card is handled.
tarjetas.detalle: Add $235,000 of life cover to reach $485,000 total; after card paydown total needed becomes $491,800.

tarjetas.frente: No umbrella policy puts a lot of savings at risk
tarjetas.reverso: Home and car insurance exist, but a big liability claim would tap your liquid savings. An umbrella policy shields the money you’re holding for the kids and big goals.
tarjetas.detalle: Recommended umbrella: $1,000,000 gap; no current umbrella policy.

tarjetas.frente: College saving is unfunded and competes with protection
tarjetas.reverso: Nothing is in the kids' college accounts yet, so extra yearly saving is needed. That money competes with paying the card and buying life cover, so pick an order that fits what matters most to both of you.
tarjetas.detalle: Total college gap: $113,508.60; extra yearly saving needed first year: $4,609.22.

siguiente_paso.razon: Clearing the high-rate card is the quickest move that the plan models to unclog your published score and stop interest draining your cash cushion.
